records.name: Penza Oblast
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: UK government country policy and information note (June 2025) sets out the national framework this Russian division stands under: same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned and the constitution offers no specific legal protections for LGBT+ people. Public expression 'promoting' non-heterosexual relationships or gender transition is punishable under the 'gay propaganda' law by fines or detention of up to 15 days, with repeated offences risking criminal prosecution and up to four years' imprisonment. Between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 people in Russia were affected by enforcement of anti-LGBT+ laws, including convictions, detentions and 'extremism' prosecutions, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023. These are the national-position facts on which this division's assessment at the national score rests.

Human Rights Watch report (30 June 2025) documents federal 'extremism' enforcement that applies nationwide, this division included: Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participating in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its alleged symbols, and 81 people in 98 court cases since January 2024 have been convicted of administrative offences for displaying those symbols, mostly on social media. It traces the 2023 Supreme Court designation of the movement as 'extremist', which enabled criminal prosecutions carrying up to 12 years in prison, building on the 2013 'gay propaganda' law. These are the national-framework repression facts supporting this division's assessment at the national score.

records.name: Leningrad oblast
records.current_summary: This division carries one documented incident beyond the national pattern: in February 2025 a gender-nonconforming person who sold sex was murdered in a local town, dismembered and the remains dumped in the river in the region's principal city; the perpetrator was arrested within days and sentenced to 11 years in a strict-regime colony in September 2025 by the local city court. The case is recorded for the institutional response - swift arrest, prosecution and a substantial sentence - while press coverage mocked and misgendered the victim. The federal repression framework (anti-propaganda and extremism laws; for foreigners, detention of up to 15 days and deportation) otherwise applies unchanged in this division.
